I found one blocking bug and one non-blocking observation in PR #71.

## Issue 1: a symlinked `~/.claude/settings.json` whose target is missing fails the unit, so the defaults are never written

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images71-p11-2/repo/images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`
- **Added line:** `ExecStart=/bin/cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json %h/.claude/settings.json`
- **Reason:** bug (plus a missing test)
- **Blocking:** yes
- **Description:** GNU `cp` refuses to write through a symlink whose target does not exist. It fails with "not writing through dangling symlink" unless `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set. The image is built on Ubuntu 26.04, whose `cp` comes from uutils. I am inferring that uutils behaves the same, because it aims to match GNU's tests (`tests/cp/thru-dangling.sh`); I did not run anything to confirm this.

  The code that runs beside this unit already handles this state. `claude-pre-approval@merge` resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the target as `{}` when it is missing. The new unit's own comment says it is meant to "write through a symlinked file (a dotfiles checkout's, say)", so a link to a file the checkout does not have yet is a state it should expect.
- **Trigger:** `~/.claude/settings.json` is a link (for example to `../dotfiles/settings.json`), the dotfiles directory exists, but `settings.json` is not in it yet. `/home/dev` is a persistent volume, so this survives across starts.
- **Path:** `images/coder-template/agent-services.target@Wants` → `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (`cp` fails, unit enters a failed state) → `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval.service` (ordered only with `Before=`, no `Requires=`, so it still runs) → `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval@merge` (creates the target as `{}`, plus `enableAllProjectMcpServers` when trust is on) → `images/coder-template/claude-remote-control.service`.
- **Outcome:** `claude-default-settings.service` ends in a failed state on that start. Remote control and every later Claude session start without the Claude default settings: no permission denies, no `defaultMode: auto`, no `model: opus`. That contradicts the PR's claim that "remote control must start with the defaults in place".
- **Suggested fix:** resolve the link the way `merge` does, e.g. `ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json)"'`. Then extend the smoke test with a case where the link exists but its target does not.

## Issue 2 (observation): `~/.claude` is now created with mode 0755 instead of 0700

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images71-p11-2/repo/images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`
- **Added line:** `ExecStartPre=/bin/mkdir -p %h/.claude`
- **Reason:** bug (minor)
- **Blocking:** no
- **Description:** This unit now runs before `claude-pre-approval`, so it is the first thing to create `~/.claude` in a fresh home. Before this PR, the pre-approval script created it under `umask 077` (when trust was on), or Claude Code created it itself. Now `mkdir` runs under the user manager's default umask of 0022, so the directory comes out 0755. A new `settings.json` also comes out 0644.
- **Trigger:** a fresh home (or a removed `~/.claude`), then the agent services start. The smoke test's last section reaches exactly this state.
- **Path:** `images/coder-template/agent-services.target@Wants` → `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service@ExecStartPre` → `images/coder-template/claude-pre-approval@merge` (its `mkdir -p` is now a no-op).
- **Outcome:** `~/.claude`, which later holds Claude's credentials file and session transcripts, is readable by other local users wherever the home directory allows it. The impact is small in a single-user workspace.
- **Suggested fix:** `mkdir -m 0700 -p` or `UMask=0077` on the unit, which would match the pre-approval script's `umask 077`.

The rest checks out: unit ordering, `RemainAfterExit` and `PartOf` reruns, the target waiting on its oneshot units, the Dockerfile copy path, and the smoke assertions (`jq` structural equality on the link's target, `cmp` on a fresh home, the link kept). No reviewer findings were dismissed in this pass.

I found no blocking correctness or security issues. There are two non-blocking points, and a list of candidates I checked and dismissed.

**1. Writing through the symlink changes the user's dotfiles checkout every start**
- File: `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.service`
- Added lines:
  - `# cp, not install: it writes through a symlinked file (a dotfiles checkout's, say) instead of replacing the link.`
  - `ExecStart=/bin/cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json %h/.claude/settings.json`
- Reason: bug / data loss. Not blocking, because the comment shows it is deliberate.
- **Trigger:** the user's `~/.claude/settings.json` is a symlink into a dotfiles git checkout. `smoke.sh` sets up exactly this with `ln -sf ../dotfiles/settings.json ~/.claude/settings.json`.
- **Path:** `agent-services.target@Wants` → `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` (cp follows the link) → `claude-pre-approval@merge` (`readlink -f`, then `mv` onto the target).
- **Outcome:** the tracked file in the dotfiles repo is rewritten to the image defaults (plus `enableAllProjectMcpServers`) at every start. The repo becomes dirty, and if the user commits or syncs it, their own settings are lost on every other machine too.
- The PR's "Merge Danger" only says edits to `~/.claude/settings.json` are overwritten. It does not say the dotfiles source file is changed.
- Suggested fix: say this in the PR body and the usage doc. Or, if the dotfiles source should stay untouched, replace the link and accept losing it.

**2. `defaultMode: auto` also applies to workspaces created for untrusted code, and users cannot keep a different value**
- File: `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.json`
- Added line: `"defaultMode": "auto"`
- Reason: security. Not blocking; this is a question.
- **Trigger:** a workspace created with `claude_trust_workspace=false`. ADR 0016 says this is the "really untrusted code" case. The user runs `claude` interactively in the repo and accepts the trust prompt.
- **Path:** `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` → `~/.claude/settings.json` `permissions.defaultMode`. `claude-pre-approval` does not depend on the trust choice for this key.
- **Outcome:** before this PR, interactive sessions started in the default mode and asked before each tool call. Now they start in auto mode, where an automatic check decides instead of the user. Any user-level change is reset at the next start, so users can only override it per project in `.claude/settings.local.json`.
- The trust choice now has no effect on permission mode. Remote control already passed `--permission-mode auto`, so only interactive sessions change.
- Suggested fix: if that is intended, say so. Otherwise, apply auto mode only when trust is on.

**Dismissed candidates** (logged as AGENTS.md requires, for human review):
- **Ordering:** `Before=` in the new unit orders it ahead of `claude-pre-approval` and `claude-remote-control`. When the target restarts, `PartOf` restarts all three units in one transaction, so the pre-approval key is always added back after the copy.
- **Revoking MCP approval when trust is switched off:** the new unit drops `enableAllProjectMcpServers` at each start, which seems to contradict ADR 0016's "nothing is ever revoked". It cannot happen, because `templates/coder/main.tf` declares `claude_trust_workspace` as `mutable = false`. Only the smoke test simulates switching it.
- **File and directory modes:** on a fresh home, `cp` creates `settings.json` as 0644, and `mkdir -p` makes `~/.claude` 0755. Before, pre-approval's `umask 077` gave 0700 when trust was on. There is no concrete exposure: the file holds only non-secret defaults, dev is the only real user, and Ubuntu's `useradd` creates `/home/dev` as 0750. If the file already exists, cp keeps its mode.
- **A failed oneshot:** if cp fails (for example, GNU cp refuses to write through a dangling symlink), the unit shows as failed. The target still starts because it only uses `Wants`, and pre-approval and remote control run without the defaults. The failure is visible in systemd and nothing else breaks.
- **Validity of the JSON keys:** the keys match the repo's own `.claude/settings.json`, apart from the `attribution.commit` text and the second plugin. I could not show that any key is invalid.
- **Restarting a unit alone:** restarting only `claude-default-settings.service` would remove the MCP approval until pre-approval runs again. That needs a manual command, so it is speculation.

CONFIRM — If `~/.claude/settings.json` is a dangling symlink, `cp` in `ExecStart` fails. GNU cp errors with "not writing through dangling symlink", and I expect uutils cp on the Ubuntu 26.04 base (`images/core/Dockerfile`) to do the same, but I couldn't check that without running anything. The unit has only `Before=` ordering and the target uses `Wants=`, so `claude-pre-approval` and remote control still start with no default settings applied.

Two caveats don't change the verdict:
- `claude-pre-approval` creates the target as `{}` only when `CLAUDE_PREAPPROVE_TRUST_WORKSPACE` is true.
- It runs after `claude-default-settings` because of that `Before=`, so the copy has already failed by then.

DROP: outcome — Writing through the symlink is the intended, tested behavior, not a fault. The service comment says `cp` is used "instead of replacing the link" so that it "writes through a symlinked file (a dotfiles checkout's, say)". The unit description says the defaults are "written over the user's at each start". `smoke.sh` lines 93-97 assert that the defaults land in the dotfiles target and that the link survives. The candidate's trigger and path hold, but the outcome is the documented design.

DROP: outcome — the Trigger and Path hold, but no one except `dev` and root can read `~/.claude` in these images, so the exposure isn't concrete.

- **Trigger:** holds. A fresh `/home/dev` has no `~/.claude`, and the Coder agent starts `agent-services.target`.
- **Path:** holds.
  - `claude-default-settings.service` has `Before=claude-pre-approval.service`, so its `ExecStartPre=/bin/mkdir -p %h/.claude` runs first.
  - It runs under the user manager's default umask, which is normally 0022.
  - `claude-pre-approval` sets `umask 077`, but its `mkdir -p` finds the directory already there.
  - So `~/.claude` is created 0755.
- **Outcome:** does not hold.
  - `images/core/Dockerfile` creates only one regular user, `dev`, with `useradd --create-home`. Nothing else in `images/` adds users.
  - `dev` already has `NOPASSWD:ALL` sudo, and root can read everything regardless of modes.
  - There is no other local user who could read the directory.
  - Ubuntu's `useradd` default `HOME_MODE` is 0750 as far as I recall; I did not check the 26.04 `login.defs`. If so, a user outside the `dev` group couldn't traverse `/home/dev` to reach `~/.claude` anyway.
  - The exposure the candidate describes is therefore only theoretical.

DROP: outcome — The ADR 0016 trust choice covers only the repository trust prompt and MCP server approval. It says nothing about permission mode, and nothing in the ADR ties trust-off to prompting before each tool call.

`defaultMode: auto` is part of the new Claude default settings. The PR adds that file as a whole, and the GLOSSARY entry and `docs/usage/coder-template.md` document that it is written over `~/.claude/settings.json` at every start. The reset of a user-level override is therefore documented too.

Auto mode is also a classifier-gated mode, not a bypass of permissions. In the untrusted-code case, ADR 0016 says the sandbox is the protection. So the candidate shows no wrong outcome or concrete security exposure.

review.body: Writing the Claude default settings at every start is well placed in the agent-services lifecycle, and the smoke test covers both a fresh home and a symlinked `~/.claude/settings.json`. One blocking issue: when `~/.claude/settings.json` is a symlink whose target does not exist yet, the copy fails and the workspace starts without the defaults. See the inline comment.

**Bug (blocking):** this fails when `~/.claude/settings.json` is a dangling symlink, for example a link into a dotfiles checkout that has no `settings.json` yet. `cp` will not write through a dangling symlink (GNU coreutils: "not writing through dangling symlink"), so this unit fails.

The failure does not stop anything else. `agent-services.target` only `Wants=` this unit, and `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service` are ordered after it with `Before=` and no `Requires=`. Both still start. Remote control and every Claude session then run without the Claude default settings: no denied tools, no `defaultMode: auto`, no `model: opus`. This state persists across starts, because `/home/dev` is a volume.

`claude-pre-approval@merge` already handles this case: it resolves the link with `readlink -f` and creates the target when it is missing. Suggested fix: resolve the link the same way, e.g.

```ini
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'cp /usr/local/share/claude-code/default-settings.json "$(readlink -f %h/.claude/settings.json)"'
```

Then add a smoke case where the link exists but its target does not.
